title: Infinite Loops and Escaping Them
objectives: Explain why a loop can run forever
Know how to avoid an infinite loop

hook.text: What happens if you forget to increase the counter inside a WHILE loop? Your computer looks frozen. In fact, it is repeating the same job forever.

concept.heading: Why does an infinite loop happen?
concept.body: If the condition of a WHILE loop NEVER becomes FALSE, the loop never ends. The most common cause is forgetting to update, inside the loop, the variable that affects the condition (for example, a missing counter ← counter + 1 line).

concept.heading: How do you avoid it?
concept.body: Every time you write a WHILE (or DO-WHILE), ask yourself: "Is there an update that will make this condition FALSE, and does that update really run?" Remember the finiteness property (lesson 0.2): an algorithm must end.

items.label: the condition becomes FALSE one day

workedExamples.prompt: The counter is never updated in this loop. What happens? (Warning: this is a deliberate example of a mistake.)
workedExamples.runnerSource:
i ← 0
WHILE i < 5
  WRITE i
END_LOOP

steps.explain: i < 5 is TRUE, so the loop is entered.
0 is written. But i NEVER changes, so the condition will stay TRUE forever!

exercises.question: Why does the loop in the worked example above never end?
options: Because i is a text variable
Because i is never updated inside the loop, so the condition stays TRUE
Because the WRITE command is wrong
Actually this loop runs 5 times and ends

feedback.correct: Correct. Since i is not updated, the condition i < 5 never becomes FALSE.
feedback.incorrect: The problem is that the variable i is never changed inside the loop, so the condition stays TRUE forever.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: When you write a WHILE loop, you must make sure the variable that affects the condition is ___ inside the loop.

exercises.question: When can "WHILE TRUE ... END_LOOP" (a loop whose condition is always TRUE) be a valid thing to use?
options: Never, it is always a mistake
When it is ended inside the loop by some other mechanism (for example, a conditional exit with an IF)
Only when used together with a FOR loop
Only when it is never run

feedback.correct: Correct. In some languages it can be used in a controlled way with an exit mechanism like "break", but that is an advanced topic and needs care.
feedback.incorrect: Deliberate infinite loops can be used if there is another ending mechanism inside, but you have to be careful.

exercises.question: Which algorithm property does an infinite loop violate?

feedback.correct: Correct. An algorithm must end at some point: the finiteness property.
feedback.incorrect: An infinite loop violates the finiteness property, which says an algorithm must end.

exercises.question: Put the debugging process for writing a WHILE loop in the correct order.
steps: Identify the condition of the loop
Find the variable that affects the condition
Check that this variable is updated inside the loop
Check that the update moves in the direction that will make the condition FALSE

exercises.question: What happens with the loop "FOR i ← 1 TO 10 STEP -1" (the step is negative but the start is smaller than the end)?
options: It never runs (the condition is not met from the start)

feedback.correct: Correct. When the step is negative and the start is smaller than the end, the loop condition is never met and the body does not run.
feedback.incorrect: In a counting loop, if the step direction does not match the start/end relationship, the loop never runs. It does not become an infinite loop.

summary: An infinite loop is a loop whose condition never becomes FALSE.
The most common cause: forgetting to update, inside the loop, the variable that affects the condition.
Every time you write a loop, ask: "will this really end?"
